title: The ceilDiv gross-up compensates the bps leg but not the share round-trip, so netGuaranteed can land below netWanted
description: previewExitFor grosses the request up with Math.ceilDiv to compensate the slippage-bps leg, but the subsequent share round-trip (convertToShares then convertToAssets) floors twice, and the ceilDiv does not compensate that. netGuaranteed can therefore land below netWanted, contradicting story-050's claimed property.
impact: Dust: at most 1 wei observed. Analytic bound netWanted - netGuaranteed <= ceil(A/S) + 2 raw base units, confirmed by a 256-run fuzz with no counterexample, reproduced at near-unity and ~3x share prices. Known-benign under the ROUNDING-DIRECTION pattern: ceilDiv rounds the REQUEST up (protocol-favouring) and the double floor rounds the QUOTE down. NO USER-FAVOURING LEG and no repeatable round-trip profit; DIVISION-PRECISION refuted (mul-before-div throughout).
attackPath: A consumer requests netWanted at a non-dividing share price with no cap binding.
The bps gross-up rounds up; the share round-trip floors twice.
netGuaranteed comes back at most 1 wei below netWanted, contradicting the story's claimed property.
No user-favouring direction exists, so there is no extractable profit.
recommendation: Either compensate the share round-trip in the gross-up (add the ceil(A/S) + 2 bound) or correct story-050's claimed property to state the dust tolerance explicitly. This is a documentation/spec correction more than a code fix.
channelNote: CHANNEL DISAGREEMENT with the source pass, resolved: severity QA is agreed, the CHANNEL is not. This is a deviation from story-050's stated behaviour, so under Law 2 it is routed to spec-conformance.md as F-17-03, NOT dropped into the QA/gas bundle. A pure behavioural deviation with no security impact is still reported where the owner will see it.
lineCitationNote: Same off-by-two as L-26: the gross-up statement is on line 176 at cdd0743, not 174.
escalationTrigger: A user-favouring rounding leg appearing on the same path, or a bound that scales with position size rather than with ceil(A/S). Neither exists today.
